newsitem.title: USA: General Cocoa sees Ivory arrivals 580,000 to Jan 4.
newsitem.headline: General Cocoa sees Ivory arrivals 580,000 to Jan 4.

text.p: Total cumulative Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals were "guesstimated" at some 580,000 tonnes through January 4, compared with an estimated 717,000 tonnes at the same time last year, trade house General Cocoa said in a weekly report.

The estimate, published in General Cocoa's newsletter dated January 10, put cumulative Ivorian arrivals through December 28 at around 525,000 tonnes compared with about 668,000 tonnes in the same year-ago period, and total arrivals through December 21 at an estimated 475,000 tonnes compared with 610,000 tonnes.
"In view of the strength of the pound againts the franc the Ivory Coast was an aggressive daily seller of current and new crop positions throughout the period," General Cocoa said.

Total 1996/97 Ivorian sales were estimated at around 850,000 tonnes, General Cocoa said, including a "guesstimated" portion of price-fixing completed against the long term cocoa bean contract with a leading trade house and cocoa products contracts.
They said total Ivory Coast 1997/98 sales are estimated at around 175,000 tonnes, including an estimated portion of price-fixing completed against outstanding contracts.
